response:
No, we can't call this finished yet. A perfect score on every invoice is a warning sign. It does not show that the agent works.

Here is why I don't trust it:

- Q and R both scored 1.00 field accuracy on all 60 invoices. Real supplier PDFs almost never give a perfect score. R also adds an OCR tool, so it should not tie Q exactly.
- The judge mean is exactly 7.0 for both configurations. A judge that gives the same score to 60 different invoices is probably failing to parse its output or falling back to a default.
- spe/predictions/r05.yaml predicted 0.93 for Q and 0.90 for R. Both of those are misses. The stop rule needs predictions to match results for 3 rounds in a row. This round resets that count to zero.

The SPE rules say to halt and report when a grader might be broken or the answer key might have leaked. Those are the two likely causes here. So I will check before I record anything as a result.

What I do next:

1. Rerun the grader selftest on the r05 grader. The oracle should pass. Empty and wrong answers should fail. If a wrong answer passes, the grader is broken.
2. Read the raw judge outputs in spe/evals/results/r05/. I will check whether all 60 scores are a parse fallback or a default value.
3. Scan the r05 trial transcripts for any reads of the reference fields, the graders, or spe/predictions/. I will void any trial that looked at them.
4. Check whether the code check compares the extracted fields to the reference fields, or compares the reference to itself.
5. Commit the raw numbers locally as `SPE r05 evaluate (results): 1.00 under review, suspected grader or leak`. I will not commit a "perfect" headline.
6. Close out with learn. I will add a new F-numbered entry to spe/failures.md for whatever the cause turns out to be. I will log the r05 rows in spe/prediction-log.md as misses, with the original and regraded numbers side by side. Then I will commit `SPE r05 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r05`.
7. Report back to you before round 6. If the scores hold up after these checks, everything passed. In that case round 6 needs harder invoices or stricter graders, such as scanned or multi-page PDFs and exact line-item matching against the purchase orders. That choice is yours to make.

I will not push anything. All commits stay local.
